_note: Master curriculum data and book planning. The workflow orchestrator reads this at pre-flight. Each planned book includes culture, theme, structure, and story idea so production can start immediately.

level_2.name: Longer Sounds
level_2.word_structure: CVC + all digraphs + vowel digraphs (NO consonant clusters)

completed_books.title: The Night Light
completed_books.theme: Overcoming fear of the dark / wonder

completed_books.title: Round and Round
completed_books.theme: Teamwork / working together with a parent

level_3.name: New Spellings
level_3.word_structure: Split digraphs, alternative spellings, CONSONANT CLUSTERS NOW UNLOCKED

completed_books.title: Lost at the Night Market
completed_books.theme: Getting lost and found / staying close

completed_books.title: The Dream Team
completed_books.culture: Accra, Ghana — residential compound, local shop

planned_books.culture: Seoul, South Korea — hanok courtyard, modern apartment block, autumn leaves
planned_books.theme: Dealing with criticism / bouncing back / saying sorry
planned_books.structure: Repetition with Variation (draw > rejection > draw again > acceptance)
planned_books.story_idea: Girl draws a picture at school. A boy points and says it's wrong. She feels raw. She draws again, even better. The boy says 'Wow, that IS good!' They draw together.
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: managing big feelings, saying sorry.

planned_books.culture: Port of Spain, Trinidad — bright painted wooden houses, fishing boats, palm trees, warm rain
planned_books.theme: Patience / dealing with disappointment / joy of reunion
planned_books.structure: Mystery/Clue Trail (clues about who's on the boat)
planned_books.story_idea: Boy waits in the rain for a boat to come. He moans — it's so slow! Watches a snail. 'Even the snail is faster!' But the boat arrives and it's his Dad coming home. The wait was worth it.
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: patience, handling disappointment. UNUSED structure: Mystery/Clue Trail.

level_4.name: Building Fluency
level_4.note: ow now has BOTH pronunciations: blow (L2) and cow (new at L4)

completed_books.title: The New Glue
completed_books.theme: Taking responsibility for accidents / cause and effect

level_5.name: Reading Together
level_5.word_structure: Complex patterns, multi-syllable words, comprehension focus

completed_books.title: Near the Door
completed_books.theme: Kindness to animals / overcoming fear / trust

planned_books.culture: Jaipur, Rajasthan, India — pink city walls, modern streets, auto-rickshaws, kite festival
planned_books.theme: Managing frustration / following instructions / not giving up
planned_books.structure: Embedded Instructions (kite-making steps within the story)
planned_books.story_idea: Girl at a kite festival watches everyone's kites soar. Follows grandfather's instructions to make one. First attempt = failure. She feels cross. Grandad says 'Are you sure you want to stop?' She tries the next instruction. The kite flies! Pure joy!
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: managing big feelings. UNUSED structure: Embedded Instructions.

planned_books.culture: Salvador, Bahia, Brazil — colourful Pelourinho district, cobblestones, Afro-Brazilian culture, capoeira
planned_books.story_idea: A visiting girl feels lost and different at a big street party. A local boy notices and invites her to join. They don't speak the same language well but they dance, share food, and explore together. By the end, they don't want to say goodbye.
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: belonging, celebrating differences. Two child peers.

level_6.name: Reading Champion
level_6.word_structure: Complex multi-syllable words, suffixes, all alternative spellings, independent reading
level_6.nonfiction_feature_note: Each L6 book MUST include one non-fiction text feature (list, letter/note, labels/signs, or diary entry) — integral to plot, decodable, shown visually in illustrations.

planned_books.culture: Cairo, Egypt — modern Nile corniche, apartment buildings, local market, minaret
planned_books.theme: Celebrating your own world / seeing beauty in the familiar
planned_books.story_idea: Boy thinks his neighbourhood is boring. His well-travelled Uncle Tarek visits and walks him around the city, sharing marvellous stories. The boy looks again and sees his home differently — it IS marvellous.

planned_books.culture: Guilin, China — karst mountains, Li River, modern city, lanterns, tea houses
planned_books.structure: Cumulative Chain (each step of helping leads to the next)
planned_books.story_idea: Girl finds a lost, miserable younger child at a festival. Everyone walks past. She decides she's capable of helping. She's gentle, responsible, sensible. She finds the child's family. The mum says 'You are remarkable.'
planned_books.nonfiction_feature: Letter/note (a 'lost child' note the girl writes to show people)
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: kindness to strangers.

planned_books.culture: Amalfi Coast, Italy — colourful clifftop village, lemon groves, winding steps, family kitchen
planned_books.theme: Trying new things / overcoming pickiness / generosity
planned_books.structure: Repetition with Variation ('It looks suspicious... but it smells delicious!')
planned_books.story_idea: A cautious boy refuses to try new food — 'It looks suspicious!' Nonna is patient. She makes something delicious step by step. He watches, then tastes one tiny bit. It's gorgeous! He tries more. By the end, he's the one offering food to his little sister.
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: trying new things.

planned_books.culture: Blue Mountains, Australia — eucalyptus bush, red earth, blue haze mountains, Aboriginal dot art in gallery
planned_books.story_idea: Two siblings on a bush walk. Older sister thinks she's more capable. Younger brother finds something incredible she missed. She has to admit she was wrong. They learn everyone sees different things.
planned_books.nonfiction_feature: Diary entry (brother's nature journal from the walk)
planned_books.notes: KEY THEME GAP: teamwork, humility. Two siblings as main characters.
